first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited memories independently indicate that simpler, shorter onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early activation. Verifying both provides the strongest basis for the single available experiment. Promotional pricing is not preferred despite competitive pressure because memory_73 reports materially worse 30-day retention, conflicting with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective.

mid.rationale: Run a standard guarded simplification experiment on the self-serve onboarding flow. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification also lifted activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. Monitor retention because the signup test showed a 1% decline, and avoid assuming the SMB-specific result generalizes to other segments.

final2.rationale: The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn conversations justify changing the cycle decision to a narrowly targeted pricing test for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts. Memory_73 indicates this segment can produce acquisition and revenue lift, but its material 30-day retention decline makes a broad rollout incompatible with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Use strict eligibility, a limited cohort, and retention and qualified-revenue guardrails; the pricing evidence remains unverified this cycle.
